summary_of_bug: BZip2CompressorInputStream.read(byte[], offset, length) returns -1 for a zero-length read when called with offset == buffer.length, even though the stream is not exhausted. The failing test shows that after successfully reading 1024 bytes, read(buffer, 1024, 0) should return 0 per InputStream semantics, and a subsequent normal read still returns data, proving the earlier -1 incorrectly signaled EOF.

COMPRESS-296.label: I
COMPRESS-296.reason: This is about parallel ZIP compression performance, which is a different subsystem and mechanism from a BZip2 input-stream `read(byte[], off, len)` return-value bug. No regional overlap beyond the broad library, and no shared stream-read boundary-condition logic.

COMPRESS-306.label: P
COMPRESS-306.reason: This involves stream factory creation and propagation of encoding into archive input/output streams. It is not the same mechanism as zero-length reads or `InputStream` contract handling, but it does touch stream-construction paths in the same general I/O/compression library. The signal is mostly structural, not functional.

COMPRESS-302.label: I
COMPRESS-302.reason: This concerns `ArchiveStreamFactory` immutability/thread-safety after adding encoding support. The mechanism is concurrency/state management in a factory, not buffer-boundary handling or `read(byte[], off, len)` semantics in `BZip2CompressorInputStream`. Very weak diagnostic value for localizing the current failure.
